s1.syndrome_frame: Acute intermittent epigastric pain and abdominal distention with systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Generalized abdominal tenderness with mild distention
Duodenal diverticula, wall thickening with mesenteric edema, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy
key_facts: 10-day history of worsening symptoms
Epigastric pain is nonradiating and cramping
Patient reports fever, chills, and anorexia
Leukocyte count is elevated at 11.4 K/CUMM
Liver function tests are normal
Lipase is within normal limits at 10 U/L
CT scan shows duodenal diverticula, wall thickening, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy
Follow-up CT scan shows resolution of inflammatory changes
Patient has a history of epilepsy and osteoporosis
Family history of ulcerative colitis

shortlist.label: Diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan shows duodenal diverticula, wall thickening, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy, consistent with diverticulitis

shortlist.label: Duodenal diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Specific location of diverticula in duodenum and symptoms of epigastric pain and abdominal distention

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Family history of ulcerative colitis and symptoms of abdominal pain, fever, and weight loss

shortlist.label: Mesenteric panniculitis
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan shows mesenteric lymphadenopathy and inflammation, consistent with mesenteric panniculitis

shortlist.label: Sclerosing mesenteritis
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan shows wall thickening and mesenteric edema, consistent with sclerosing mesenteritis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of epigastric pain, fever, chills, and anorexia, combined with the CT scan findings of duodenal diverticula, wall thickening, and mesenteric lymphadenopathy, are consistent with duodenal diverticulitis. The follow-up CT scan showing resolution of inflammatory changes also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Diverticulitis
rejected.why: While diverticulitis is a possible diagnosis, the specific location of the diverticula in the duodenum makes duodenal diverticulitis a more precise diagnosis.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: There is no evidence of chronic inflammation or other typical features of Crohn's disease, such as weight loss or changes in stool caliber.

rejected.label: Mesenteric panniculitis
rejected.why: The CT scan findings do not show the characteristic fat necrosis and inflammation of the mesenteric fat seen in mesenteric panniculitis.

rejected.label: Sclerosing mesenteritis
rejected.why: The CT scan findings do not show the characteristic fibrosis and sclerosis of the mesenteric fat seen in sclerosing mesenteritis.
